articles.title: GHSA: qbee-agent: Docker Compose build context Zip Slip writes outside context directory
articles.summary:
## Summary

`qbee-agent` contains a Zip Slip vulnerability in `app/utils/tar.go`. The tar extractor checks whether an entry remains inside the destination directory with:

```go

```

articles.title: GHSA: Silverstripe Framework: RCE via i18nTextCollectorTask writer parameter
articles.summary:
### Impact
The writer option of the i18nTextCollectorTask dev task was passed to the injector without validation. A crafted dev task URL could create arbitrary objects with attacker-controlled constructor arguments and run code on the server. Because the dev task did not ask for confirmation, an administrator could be tricked into running it by following a link. On a site in dev mode, no login was

articles.title: GHSA: Silverstripe Framework: User-controlled ClassName allows unauthorized record type change
articles.summary:
### Impact
A user who can edit a record through a GridField detail form could change the record to an unrelated class, without the permission checks for that class.

### Reported by
Lachlan Davidson, Carapace

articles.title: GHSA: Silverstripe Framework: CMS_ACCESS_SecurityAdmin privilege escalation
articles.summary:
### Impact
A user with access to the Security section (CMS_ACCESS_SecurityAdmin) but without the ADMIN permission could edit a group that grants ADMIN through a role or a parent group, and use it to escalate their own privileges.

### Reported by
Lachlan Davidson, Carapace

articles.title: GHSA: Silverstripe Framework: Auth bypass GridFieldDetailForm
articles.summary:
### Impact
A CMS user who can edit records through a GridField detail form could create new records without the permission to create them, by sending a save request directly.

### Reported by
HDWSec - https://hdwsec.fr

articles.title: GHSA: Silverstripe Framework: XSS via SVG data URI
articles.summary:
### Impact
The HTML sanitiser did not remove SVG data URIs. A CMS author could store content that runs JavaScript in the browser of another user who views it.

### Reported by
HDWSec - https://hdwsec.fr

articles.title: GHSA: Silverstripe Framework: XSS via XHTML data URI
articles.summary:
### Impact
The HTML sanitiser did not remove XHTML and XML data URIs. A CMS author could store content that runs JavaScript in the browser of another user who views it.

### Reported by
Jack Wallace from Bastion Security

articles.title: GHSA: Directus: Share update allows reassigning user_created and role
articles.summary:
### Summary

A non-admin user who can update their own shares can reassign a share's creator (`user_created`), `role`, `item`, and `collection` fields after the share is created. The update is authorized against the row as it existed before the change, and the resulting row is never revalidated, so these fields can be set to values the user would not be permitted to assign when creating a share. articles.title: GHSA: mail-parser: One hostile attachment aborts `write_attachments()` and silently drops the rest of the batch
articles.summary:
### Impact

`write_attachments()` called `_safe_attachment_filename()` and `write_sample()` inside its loop
with no guard, so a single crafted attachment raised out of the whole save. Every attachment
**after** the malicious one was silently never written, with no error surfaced to a caller that
catches only `MailParserError`.

articles.summary:

large enough to push the timestamp past the int64 epoch range, raises an exception that is
**outside the `MailParser*` hierarchy**. A caller that catches only mail-parser exceptions
does not catch it, and the parse of the entire message is aborted — the same class of issue

articles.summary:
### Summary

Two regular expressions used while parsing email headers backtrack
polynomially on attacker-controlled input. Parsing a single small, well-formed
email can consume minutes to hours of CPU, denying service to any process that
parses untrusted mail.

When using the webpack or rspack builder, the dev server serves built client chunks to any request whose `Host` header matches its `Origin`/`Referer`, or that carries `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`. articles.title: GHSA: Nuxt: Incomplete fix for GHSA-6gq8-jgmh-3ffp: an encoded slash (`%2F`) in the request path bypasses route rules on catch-all page routes
articles.summary:
### Summary

Nuxt matches route rules against the request path with encoded slashes (`%2F`) left encoded, while the page router decodes them into route params. A request that spells a slash as `%2F` can therefore render a page through a catch-all route without the route rules configured for the path it resolves to. articles.title: GHSA: SvelteKit: Build-time server-only module import guard could fail, resulting in server secrets being statically replaced in client bundle
articles.summary: Under certain circumstances, server-only imports, which typically cannot be included in the client bundle, could make their way into it, potentially exposing secrets. This could only occur when those server-only imports were made through `src/params.js`.

articles.title: GHSA: SvelteKit: DoS while parsing form data from a remote functions `form`
articles.summary: This only affects applications using the experimental remote functions flag and utilizing the `form`, `query`, or `command` remote functions. A specially-crafted request could block the event loop for extended periods of time during parsing.

articles.title: GHSA: AIOHTTP: Base64 multipart parts bypass client_max_size
articles.summary:
### Summary

When reading a multipart part with `Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64`, `BodyPartReader.read_chunk()` kept reading until the chunk length was a multiple of 4, with no byte limit. A part with a short `Content-Length`, or a long run of whitespace, could cause the entire remaining body to be read into memory within a single call before any size check, or spin on the event loop.

The `max_msg_size` check in the WebSocket reader added the declared frame length to the size of the partial message already buffered. In the C extension this addition is 64-bit arithmetic, so a declared length close to 2**63 overflowed and the check passed.

articles.summary:
### Summary

When the pipelined request queue was full, the pure-Python parser stored the unparsed remainder internally and also returned it to the caller. After a handler declined an upgrade request, the buffered data was re-fed, so the buffer grew with each handled request and already-handled requests were dispatched to the application again.

articles.summary:
### Summary

When decompressing a payload made up of many concatenated compressed members (gzip, deflate or zstd), each member was decoded by passing the entire remaining input to a new decompressor, resulting in quadratic CPU time. Empty members produce no output, so `client_max_size` and output backpressure did not limit the work.

articles.title: GHSA: SvelteKit: Private `query.batch` functions could collide, producing unexpected parameter / function combinations
articles.summary: Under certain circumstances, private (non-exported) `query.batch` functions could end up sharing a batch, resulting in the arguments from one function being passed to another. This only affects apps using the experimental remote functions flag and non-exported `query.batch` functions.

articles.title: GHSA: SvelteKit: Protocol-relative module import during server-side route resolution allows cross-origin script execution
articles.summary: If an attacker could, using some form of social engineering or other exploit, get a user to use client-side navigation to navigate to a specially-crafted link, the attacker could cause code from another domain to be imported and run on the user's machine. This only affected apps with `router.resolution: 'server'`.
